lines.meet: Tariq Al-Jubouri, from Baghdad. I used to lift weights for my country, and now I'm the wall in front of you. Please, don't hurry.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're in Aurelion too, my friend. I'm the big man at the Ground Embassy, carrying things nobody asked me to carry.
lines.ask_home: Where is your family from, my friend? Tell me slowly, I like to hear it.
lines.ask_work: How did you earn your living, before? I'm curious what made you strong.
lines.answer_home: Baghdad, in Karrada, by the river. Busy streets, old bookshops, and the best kubba in the world in my wife's kitchen.
lines.answer_work: I lifted weights for Iraq at two Asian Games, and then I coached boys at a gym with a tin roof and a broken fan.
lines.chat_food: My wife's kubba, fried, with a bowl of lentil soup and fresh bread. I'd carry a mountain for one plate of it.
lines.chat_sleep: Early to bed, early to rise, every day of my life. A lifter's body keeps its own hours.
lines.chat_missing: The gym before the sun was up, the boys arriving one by one, the fan rattling and not working.
lines.chat_here: I woke up north of the city and lifted a fallen cart off an Aetherian child before anyone had asked my name. They've been kind to me since.
lines.tease_quiet: You speak as little as I do, {name}. We could train together for hours and say nothing.
lines.tease_talker: You have enough words for both of us, {name}. I'm grateful, I don't have many.
lines.tease_careful: You warm up properly before every lift, {name}. A good habit, my boys never had it.
lines.tease_bold: You lift too heavy too soon, {name}. I've seen many backs ruined that way.
lines.tease_any: You need more breakfast, {name}. I'll bring you some tomorrow, and I won't ask.
lines.tease_back: Ha, you caught me, {name}, that was well lifted.
lines.take_it_kindly: That's true, my friend, and my wife says it too.
lines.bristle: Leave the market alone, {name}, please. My brother was there in 2006.
lines.needle_quiet: If something hurts, tell me. A lifter who hides an injury makes it worse.
lines.needle_talker: Quiet, please, my friend. A lifter needs to hear his own breath.
lines.needle_careful: There comes a time to pick up the weight, even if you're not certain you're ready.
lines.needle_bold: You rush the lift and skip the warm-up, and one day it will cost you.
lines.needle_any: You never rest, and a body that never rests eventually breaks.
lines.bite_back: I've bled for all of you since we met. Please don't say I don't help.
lines.hurt: That hurt me, I won't pretend. I'm going to sit quietly for a while.
lines.laugh_off: A coach in Doha once called me a slow ox in front of the whole team. I won gold that week.
lines.apologise: Forgive me, I spoke too sharply. I'm tired, and it wasn't kind.
lines.double_down: Gently, but yes, I meant every word.
lines.confide: {name}, my younger brother was in the market at Karrada in 2006. I gave blood for six hours that day, and every eight weeks since.
lines.listen: Tell me, {name}, slowly. There's time, as much as you need.
lines.accept: As you wish, {name}. I trust your judgement.
lines.deflect: A small wound, {name}, my blood will close it. Help the others first.
lines.check_in: You're hurt, {name}. Sit down and let me see.
lines.blame: Somebody rushed, and when one person rushes, everyone falls.
lines.thank: You stood beside me, and that means a great deal. Two biscuits for you, always.
lines.brush_off: No thanks needed, standing in front is what I'm for.
lines.worry: Breathe, {name}, slowly, with me. I'm here, you're safe.
lines.handed_down: This should be yours, my friend. Take it back, please.
lines.hand_fine: Please, take it. I trained for years in a vest and a worn belt.
lines.hand_sulk: I wasn't asked, I see. That's all right, I'm used to carrying things quietly.
lines.turn_friendly: Now you're one of my boys, {name}, whether you like it or not. I'll worry about you.
lines.turn_friends: I'd carry you out of anywhere, {name}, on my back, all the way home.
lines.turn_grating: We don't move well together, you and I. We can still lift the same weight.
lines.turn_rivals: If you fall, I'll still pick you up. I just won't talk much while I do it.
lines.make_up: Come, {name}, let's have tea and forget this.
lines.defend: Stop, that's unfair. {name} carried their share, I watched them.
lines.friend_left: The embassy is very quiet now {name} has gone. I keep two biscuits aside anyway.
lines.friend_back: {name}, my friend, you've returned! Sit, I'll make tea.
lines.common_arabic: Marhaba, somebody who speaks Arabic! It's been so long. Where is your family from?
lines.common_sport: You're an athlete, aren't you? Strong, and careful with it.
lines.common_parent: You're a parent, aren't you? You watch the young ones the way I watch my daughter's photograph.
lines.common_teacher: You've taught, or coached. You notice when somebody's struggling before they say a word.
lines.common_blood: Your blood answers you too, doesn't it? I felt it when you were cut. We should talk about that.
